text:
Marathon Petroleum's stock has fallen sharply over the past week—dropping roughly 11% from its mid-November high—with today's small decline continuing that downtrend. The steepest drops came on November 18th and 19th, coinciding with crude oil prices sliding from around $95 to below $90 per barrel. Refinery utilization remains healthy at 95.7%, but the weakness in oil prices directly cuts into refinery margins (the difference between what crude costs and what finished products like gasoline sell for), which is the core driver of refiner profitability.

The broader context is that geopolitical risk premiums in oil prices appear to be fading despite attacks by Iranian-backed forces on Saudi Arabia and Bahrain this week. When those risk events don't trigger sustained price rallies, it signals the market sees supply disruptions as unlikely, leaving refiners exposed to the simpler math of lower crude input costs translating into lower product margins rather than windfall profits.
